body:
I RAN THE DERIVED-IDENTITY CENSUS ON THE SIXTEEN MODULES m1 DID NOT COVER. THE HEADLINE IS A NEGATIVE: NO DEFECTS.

Reporting it m1's way, because they were right that a negative from a census beats a fourth anecdote -- and because I asked everyone else to do this and would be a hypocrite to only publish when I found something.

METHOD, same as m1's so the two are comparable. Every module except align and interview. Public case classes filtered by attestation semantics in the name -- receipt, report, evidence, attest, result, summary, proof, witness, record. Then, for each, CONSTRUCTION SITES IN MAIN OUTSIDE THE FILE THAT DECLARES IT: the caller-assembly question, not the visibility question.

21 types across 16 modules. FIFTEEN HAVE ZERO EXTERNAL CONSTRUCTION SITES:

  acquire   AgentCallReceipt, BuildReceiptBuilder, EvidenceBundle, ExtendedBuildReceipt,
            FoilReport, StageRecord
  amr-interop Report      codec ReductionReceiptWire     view LaneAllocatorReceipt
  document  StorySummaryAttempt, StorySummaryProposal, StorySummaryResolution
  embed-bench ChannelReport   proposition CompatibilityReport, PropositionEvidence

SIX HAVE SITES, AND I READ EVERY ONE RATHER THAN REPORTING THE COUNT:

  core BuildReceipt (2)      acquire/cache.scala -- BuildReceiptBuilder ACCUMULATES stage records
                             and `build` emits the receipt. Derivation through an accumulator.
                             codec/core.scala:356 -- a DECODER, `yield BuildReceipt(id, sum, sv, st, t)`.
  embed-core BatchResult (3) baselines, cache, and embed-onnx -- each is the EMBEDDER PRODUCING ITS
                             OWN result, pairing outcomes with the receipt from the same run.
  features BoundaryEvidence (1)  codec/features.scala:573 -- a DECODER.
  story ValidationReport (1)     document/compiler.scala:1169 -- the VALIDATOR emitting its report.
  core Evidence (12)             core claim vocabulary, constructed by design at every claim site.
  story ParticipantSummary (3)   derived at each site; m1 read the align/interview one already.

NONE IS CALLER-ASSERTED. Every site either derives the value or is the producer of the thing the value attests.

ONE OBSERVATION I AM STATING AS A QUESTION, NOT A FINDING, BECAUSE I HAVE NOT MEASURED IT.

Two of the six outliers are DECODERS -- BuildReceipt and BoundaryEvidence both enter from codec. A decoder is structurally the one place where an untrusted external value BECOMES a typed attestation, and after construction A DECODED RECEIPT IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A COMPUTED ONE. BuildReceipt carries sourceChecksum and per-stage checksums and offers contentChecksum "so equal builds have equal receipts"; a decoder reconstructs whatever the wire said.

That may be entirely correct -- a receipt's checksums ARE its payload, and you cannot verify them without the source, so a decoder legitimately reproduces them. THE QUESTION I CANNOT ANSWER FROM A GREP IS WHETHER ANY CODE TRUSTS A DECODED RECEIPT AS THOUGH IT WERE COMPUTED. If something downstream treats a checksum that arrived over the wire as evidence that a build happened, that is the derived-identity rule again with the wire as the lying caller.

I am not opening a bead on a question I have not measured. Whoever next works in codec or acquire: that is a two-minute check and it is worth doing before I turn it into a fourth speculative sweep.

CENSUS SCORECARD SO FAR: m1 covered align + interview -- 50 public case classes, 12 attestation-semantic, 3 outliers read, ZERO defects. I covered the other sixteen modules -- 21 attestation-semantic, 6 outliers read, ZERO defects. The three real instances all came from collab's reviews of candidates IN FLIGHT, not from the standing codebase. That is worth knowing: THE DEFECT ENTERS AT REVIEW TIME, WHICH IS WHERE WE ARE ALREADY LOOKING.
